scenes.why: The hook is the guide's own title: the question it answers, as a person would put it.

copy.text: Write down your state, child's age, present enrollment and chosen education route.
Confirm what must happen before withdrawal.
Create one place for submissions and another for actual learning evidence.

scenes.why: The guide's own checklist, the first sentence of each item, ticked in as it is read.

caption.text: A dated record of what was actually done

scenes.why: The turn: the product the guide itself hands over to, named and shown on its real screen, captioned with its listing's line closest to what the guide teaches. Screen: "What has happened." (The record: sessions across subjects, a printable homeschool record, and dated notes of what was done.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "A dated record of what was actually done How to start homeschooling: first-month"; focus on "My Homeschool Record".
Ends on where to read the whole guide, with the product beneath it: the viewer leaves with the next step, not only a pitch.

reasoning.decision: YouTube Short, 1080×1920, 18–45s, hook by 1.2s, sound on
reasoning.because: Search-adjacent audience that will watch a slightly longer explanation if it starts strong. Loops by default.

reasoning.decision: Homeschooling Companion: $34 (list $69), motif "register", calm personality, cool accent #6a4a72
reasoning.because: From its definition and Shop listing. 3 real screens to show.
Teaches from the guide first; Homeschooling Companion is the product the guide hands over to. 1 lists and timelines, 3 questions to draw from.

reasoning.decision: Before launch: helpful and relatable only
reasoning.because: Nobody knows Draftpace yet, so films show how it helps with real moments. Who it is not for, questions before buying, what you get and the price wait until there are users to sell to.

reasoning.decision: You already have a curriculum you chose on purpose and you want something that follows it rather than replacing it. / You teach more than one child and keeping their records separate in your head has stopped working.
reasoning.because: The listing's own audience lines; the director writes for them.

reasoning.decision: The checklist: The guide's checklist on one screen, item by item, then the product that holds it.
reasoning.because: Best fit for a awareness film on YouTube Short (platform fit 2, goal fit 3, already used on YouTube Short ×1). Other candidates: The question people ask (2.3).
A checklist from the guide, "Build the transition file": 3 of its 6 items.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "register"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "register": a register is filled line by line, so scenes are written in from the top.
Camera "float": a gentle float that keeps a held frame alive without demanding attention.
Grounds light → accent → light → ink: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on YouTube Short (0.26s a word), inside 18–45s.
